slides.title: What Is a Constructor?
slides.content: A constructor is a special method that runs automatically when you create an object with 'new'. It has no return type and its name must match the class name. Constructors initialize fields and set default state.

options: Every time any method is called
When an object is created with 'new'
exercise.answer: When an object is created with 'new'

slides.title: Default Constructor
slides.content: If you do not write any constructor, C# provides a parameterless default constructor that does nothing. You can also write your own to set initial values for fields.

exercise.prompt: If no constructor is defined, C# generates a ______ constructor that takes no arguments.

slides.title: Parameterized Constructors
slides.content: You can pass arguments to a constructor, allowing each object to start with different values. This creates constructor overloads when combined with a parameterless version.

exercise.prompt: Complete the constructor so it accepts a name and sets the Name field. Starter code has the class and fields already defined.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: class
When run, your code should output: Bob

slides.title: The this Keyword
slides.content: When a constructor parameter has the same name as a class field, use 'this.field' to refer to the field and plain 'param' for the parameter. This avoids ambiguity.

exercise.prompt: Which line correctly uses 'this' to assign a parameter to a field?

slides.title: Constructor Chaining with this()
slides.content: One constructor can call another constructor in the same class using 'this(args)' in the declaration. This lets you reuse initialization logic and avoid duplication.

exercise.prompt: To chain to another constructor in the same class, use ': _____' before the constructor body.

slides.title: Constructor Chaining in Inheritance
slides.content: In a class hierarchy, the derived class constructor calls the base class constructor using 'base(args)'. If you omit it, the parameterless base constructor is called automatically.

exercise.prompt: How do you explicitly call a base class constructor from a derived class constructor?

slides.title: Static Constructors
slides.content: A static constructor (static + class name, no parameters, no access modifiers) runs once per type before any instance is created or any static member is accessed. It is typically used to initialize static fields.

exercise.prompt: Write a static constructor that sets the static Version field to "2.0".
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: static, Library()
When run, your code should output: 2.0

slides.title: Primary Constructors (C# 12)
slides.content: C# 12 introduced primary constructors for classes. Parameters listed in the class declaration can be used to initialize the class, reducing boilerplate for simple types.

exercise.prompt: Which syntax declares a primary constructor in C# 12?
options: public class Person { public Person(string name) { } }
